transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I feel like the future has just kind of closed in on me, like there isn’t much to look forward to anymore. It just feels like I'm stuck, and I can't seem to see a way out of this flat routine.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been at least two years, or did it start after a specific stressful event?

Yes, it’s been going on steadily for a little over two years now. It really started a few months after my bank merged with a larger institution, which completely changed my job and felt so overwhelming. Ever since then, I just haven't been able to shake this heavy feeling.

Since these feelings started after the job merger, have your symptoms been present most days for over two years without a period of feeling back to normal, or did they mainly come and go around that stressful event?

They have definitely been present most days, without really letting up. I haven't had any period where I felt back to my normal self over these past two years. It has just been a constant, steady weight.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or has it mainly been feeling down and stuck?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love, like pottery, hiking, and gardening—now they just feel like exhausting chores. Even when my daughter calls with good news, it doesn't bring me any happiness; it just sort of bounces off me.

During these past two years, have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt? And have these symptoms made it hard for you to work or manage daily life?

I haven't noticed major changes in my sleep or appetite, but my energy and concentration have been terrible. I feel like I'm moving through molasses with constant mind fog, which has led to poor performance reviews at work and caused me to completely neglect my house, garden, and friends. It has made managing daily life incredibly hard.

Over the past two years, have you had any periods of at least two weeks where your mood was especially low or you lost interest in nearly everything, with symptoms like sleep or appetite changes, feeling worthless or guilty, or thoughts that life wasn’t worth living?

No, it hasn't come in distinct periods or spikes; it has just been a constant, steady grayness for the entire two years. I haven't experienced things like thoughts of ending my life, feeling worthless, or major changes in my sleep or appetite. It's really just been a continuous, draining lack of energy and feeling like the future is closed in.
Have you ever had any family members with long-lasting depression, and have you ever had any periods of unusually high energy, needing much less sleep, or feeling overly confident or irritable?
I'm not aware of any family history of depression, to be honest. And no, I've never had any of those periods of unusually high energy, needing less sleep, or feeling overly confident.
Since the job merger, have your symptoms continued even after you adjusted to the change, or do they mainly happen when you feel stressed about it?

They have continued constantly, regardless of how stressed I am. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling almost every single day, even on weekends when I am away from the bank. It doesn't seem to come and go with the stress anymore; it is just always there.
Have you been able to identify a specific ongoing stressor that still explains these symptoms, or do they continue even when that stressor is no longer affecting you?

Yes, the stress from that bank merger is still very active and affects me every single day. My job changed from collaborative financial counseling into a high-pressure, quota-driven environment with strict sales targets. Coping with those relentless demands day in and day out completely drains me, leaving me with absolutely no energy for anything else.

Do you feel your symptoms are mainly a reaction to the ongoing work stress, and do they improve when you are away from that stress or on vacation? Or do they stay just as low even when the stress is not present?

While the work stress definitely started this, the heavy feeling doesn't go away even when I am away from the bank. I even planned an art-and-foliage road trip to the Shenandoah Valley, but it just felt like a heavy obligation rather than something to look forward to. Good news or simply being away from work doesn't lift my mood at all; the grayness is always there.

When you think about the job merger and the ongoing work demands, do your symptoms feel clearly tied to that stressor and its effects, or do they seem to persist as a low mood and loss of interest even when the stressor is not on your mind?

While the bank merger and work stress definitely triggered everything, the low mood and lack of interest have taken on a life of their own now. Even when I am completely away from work and trying to focus on other things, like talking to my daughter, the heavy, gray feeling persists. It doesn't seem tied to my thoughts about the job anymore; it's just always there.
In the past two years, have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, thoughts of hurting yourself, or any plans to end your life?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel incredibly hopeless and like everything is pointless, I've never had any desire to actually harm myself.

In the last two years, have you had periods when the depression was so severe that you could barely function, or symptoms like marked changes in sleep, appetite, or strong feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

No, I haven't really experienced those specific symptoms like major changes in my sleep, appetite, or feelings of guilt. But while I still manage to drag myself to work, my overall functioning has definitely suffered because I feel constantly drained. I've just let my home life, hobbies, and social connections slide completely.

Have there been any times during these two years when you felt completely back to normal for at least a few months, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, there haven't been any breaks or times when I felt back to normal at all. This heavy feeling and loss of interest have been going on pretty steadily and continuously since a few months after the bank merger. It's just been a constant weight for a little over two years now.

Do your low mood and loss of interest feel like a persistent condition that has been present nearly every day for more than two years, or do they mainly occur as a reaction to the ongoing work stress and improve when the stress is removed?

It definitely feels like a persistent condition that has been with me nearly every day for over two years now, rather than just a reaction to work stress. Even when I am completely away from the bank, like on weekends or when trying to plan a vacation, this heavy feeling doesn't lift and everything still feels like a massive obligation.
Have you ever had any periods of at least two months during these past two years when your mood and interest in things felt back to normal, or has it been present nearly every day the whole time?
No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all, not even for a few weeks, let alone two months. It has been present steadily and nearly every single day for the entire two years without any relief.

Have you had any period of at least 2 weeks during these past two years when you felt clearly depressed most of the day nearly every day, or has it mostly been a long-lasting low mood without a distinct major depressive episode?

It has mostly been a long-lasting, steady low mood rather than coming in distinct, severe two-week episodes. This heavy, gray feeling has been pretty constant and hasn't really let up or changed in intensity since it first started after the merger. It has just been one continuous, unchanging stretch for the last two years.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks during these past two years when you felt clearly depressed most of the day nearly every day, or has it mostly been a long-lasting low mood without a distinct major depressive episode?

It has definitely been a steady, continuous low mood for over two years rather than a separate, distinct episode. This heavy, gray feeling has been pretty constant and steady since a few months after the bank merger, without any real breaks.

Do you feel your low mood and loss of interest are mainly a response to the ongoing work stress, or have they stayed present nearly every day even when you are away from work and not thinking about it?

Yes, while those feelings initially seemed tied to the work stress, they have now become a constant presence. Even when I am away from work on weekends or trying to plan things I used to enjoy, that heavy, gray feeling and lack of interest persist nearly every day.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during the past two years when your mood and interest felt back to normal, or has the low mood been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. The low mood has been present nearly every single day for a little over two years now, without any periods where I felt back to my normal self. It has just been a steady, continuous weight ever since it started after the merger.
Over the past two years, have you had any periods of at least two months when you felt back to your normal self, or has the low mood been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any periods like that at all where I felt back to my normal self, certainly not for two months. This heavy, gray feeling has been a steady, continuous presence nearly every single day for a little over two years now.
Over the past two years, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or physical slowing/restlessness, even if they were mild?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite. However, I do feel physically heavy and slowed down, almost like I'm constantly trying to move through molasses.

Over the past two years, have you had any periods of at least two weeks when you felt especially depressed or lost interest in nearly everything, with other symptoms like sleep or appetite changes, guilt, or thoughts that life wasn’t worth living?

No, I haven't had any distinct, more severe waves like that over the last two years; the low mood and lack of interest have just been pretty constant and steady. I also haven't really experienced those specific other symptoms, like appetite changes or thoughts of ending my life. It has just been the same continuous gray feeling the entire time.
Did your symptoms start within a few months of the stressful job merger and have they been directly tied to that stressor, or did they continue for more than 6 months after you had adjusted to it?

My symptoms did start a few months after the merger, which was about two and a half years ago, and they have been steady ever since. I never actually adjusted to the changes at work; instead, the stress and this low mood have just been a constant, ongoing grind for over two years now.
Have your symptoms improved at all during times when the work stress was lighter or when you were away from the job for a while, or have they stayed just as constant even then?

They have stayed completely constant, with no improvement even when I am away from the job. I even tried planning a road trip to the Shenandoah Valley, but it just felt like a heavy obligation rather than a relaxing break. Being away from the bank doesn't lift this weight at all.
Have your symptoms stayed present even after the job merger stress became less intense, or do they mainly come and go in direct response to ongoing work stress?

They have stayed completely constant rather than coming and going in waves. Even though the merger happened quite a while ago, this heavy feeling and lack of energy have remained a continuous, daily presence. It doesn't seem to fluctuate based on the stress of the day anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or physical slowing/restlessness over this time, even if they were mild?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite. But I do feel physically heavy and slow, like I'm constantly moving through molasses, though I'm not sure if that's exactly what you mean.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks during these past two years when your depression became clearly worse, with symptoms like marked loss of appetite, sleep changes, feeling worthless or guilty, or thoughts that life wasn’t worth living?

No, it has just been a continuous, steady gray feeling rather than having any sudden, severe drops. I haven't experienced those specific changes in my sleep or appetite, and I've never had thoughts of ending my life. It just stays at the same constant, heavy level.
Did you first start feeling this way before age 21, or has this low mood only been present in adulthood?
No, this is definitely a recent development in my adulthood. I never felt anything like this when I was younger or before age 21. It only started about two years ago, following the bank merger.

Did your symptoms start only after the stressful job merger and stay closely tied to that stress, or did they continue for months after you had adjusted and even when the stress was no longer the main issue?

They started a few months after the bank merger, which was over two years ago, and have been steady and constant ever since. While the stressful, quota-driven environment at the bank is still ongoing, these feelings have become a continuous baseline for me. They persist even when I am at home, on weekends, or completely away from the immediate stress of the job.
